title: Bear Case Stress-Test: Customer Concentration Risks, Apple RF Renewal, and Antitrust Clouds
subtitle: A rigorous risk analysis modeling downside scenarios: hyperscaler ASIC insourcing, Apple modem independence, and regulatory scrutiny.
summary: No institutional equity memo is complete without a rigorous stress-test. Here, we model three critical headwinds: Apple's internal silicon roadmap, customer concentration among three top hyperscalers, and antitrust pushback against VMware licensing.
content:
RISK ASSESSMENT & BEAR SCENARIO Downside Floor: $1,350

While our base case remains bullish at $2,100, institutional investors must understand AVGO's tail risks: customer concentration where just two hyperscalers and Apple account for over 35% of total revenues.

1. The Apple Dependency: The FBAR Filter & RF Dilemma

For over a decade, Apple has represented roughly 20% of Broadcom’s aggregate revenue through wireless radio frequency (RF) components, FBAR filters, and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth combo chips.

Apple's multi-year initiative to design custom cellular modems and RF front-ends remains the greatest single-customer risk factor on AVGO's 10-K filing. Although Broadcom signed a multi-billion dollar extension in 2023 for FBAR filters, any loss of socket share in future iPhone generations represents an immediate 400-600 bps headwind to consolidated gross margins.

Risk Matrix Placeholder 4.1

Customer Revenue Concentration Matrix (% of FY24 Revenues)

Apple Inc. (Wireless RF, Wi-Fi, Custom Filters) ~18.5% of Total Net Rev
Hyperscaler A (Google TPU Co-Design) ~11.0% of Total Net Rev
Hyperscaler B (Meta MTIA Custom ASIC) ~7.5% of Total Net Rev

Top 3 customers account for ~37% of Broadcom's aggregate top-line revenue.

2. Hyperscaler ASIC Insourcing Threat

While Broadcom currently assists Google in designing and manufacturing TPU v5e/v6 and Meta in building MTIA, hyperscalers continually harbor ambitions of full in-house silicon independence (disintermediation).

Should Google or Meta succeed in directly liaising with TSMC for packaging without Broadcom's physical design and SerDes IP, AVGO’s AI semiconductor growth would decelerate markedly from 30%+ to mid single digits.

3. Regulatory Scrutiny in the EU and North America

European enterprise user groups (such as CISPE) have lodged formal complaints with the European Commission regarding VMware's contract restructuring, citing steep price hikes and alleged anti-competitive bundling. While antitrust fines have historically been manageable for Broadcom, severe regulatory remedies could restrict future M&A targets.

4. Downside Valuation Scenario: The $1,350 Floor

In our severe bear case model, we assume:

  • Apple RF content declines 50% by FY27 as Apple's in-house modem scales.
  • Custom ASIC gross margins compress by 400 bps due to TSMC foundry price increases.
  • Broadcom forward multiple compresses from 28x to 19x (historical semiconductor cyclical average).

Under this scenario, AVGO FY26 EPS estimates drop to $71.00, yielding a target price of $1,350.00 (-24.2% downside). We assign a 20% probability to this stress scenario, reinforcing our base-case asymmetric risk/reward.
